clips.send: The dam leaves the water upstream about 113 m higher than downstream. Ships have two ways up: one, the double-lane, five-step ship locks (双线五级船闸) — a staircase of 5 water “steps” that takes several big ships at once but needs about 3½ hours; two, the ship lift (升船机) — a giant elevator, about 40 minutes, but one ship of up to 3,000 tons at a time. Tap a ship, then tap “Locks” or “Lift”.

clips.send: A lock chamber is a giant pool with a gate at each end. The ship sails in, the gate behind it closes, and water from upstream flows in through tunnels, lifting the water — and the ship. When the water is level with the next step, the pressure on both sides of the gate is equal and the gate can swing open. If the levels differ, thousands of tons of water press the gate shut.
